Assurance regime; jurisdiction UK/US/EU

Financial statement audit

The closest structural precedent for lab-paid evaluation. Independence was engineered by standards, inspection of auditors, rotation, and liability rather than by changing who pays.

Audit committee of independent directors selects since 2002; PCAOB inspects auditors.

Payer, access, publication

Who pays. Audited company pays the auditor; audit committee hires and fires (post-2002).
Access. Full access to books, records, management, and staff under statute and professional standards.
Publication. Auditor's opinion is public; working papers are confidential; PCAOB inspection reports partly public.

1933mandateUS Securities Act and 1934 Exchange Act require independent audits for listed companies after the 1929 crash.3source
1934publication ruleAudited financial statements filed publicly with the SEC.2source
1938triggerMcKesson & Robbins fraud: auditors had not verified inventory or receivables.integrity_failure: Audit failed to detect fabricated inventory and receivablessource
1939standardsFirst Statements on Auditing Procedure: physical inventory observation and receivables confirmation become required.2source
1990delegationAudit firms' consulting revenue from audit clients overtakes audit fees at large firms.source
2001triggerEnron collapse; Arthur Andersen had provided audit and consulting services to the same client.financial_loss: Losses above $1B; auditor complicitsource
2002accreditationPCAOB registers and inspects audit firms.4source
2002independence ruleSarbanes-Oxley: PCAOB created to inspect auditors; audit and most consulting separated; lead partner rotation every five years; audit committee independence.4source
2014independence ruleEU audit reform: mandatory firm rotation and a cap on non-audit fees for public-interest entities.4source
